findings.headline: Early‑race stress high but pace unchanged – keep current plan
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 64.7 on lap 6 while on dry medium tyres (age 6) and the driver was 1.5 s off the car ahead in P3. The model shows negligible degradation (+0.174 s/lap) and pace delta was -0.222 s, so the high stress did not translate into slower laps. No strategy change is needed; monitor but keep the current plan.

findings.headline: Grip loss on lap 19‑22 caused major slowdown – timing of intermediate switch was optimal
findings.detail: During the wet‑to‑dry transition (lap 19‑22) the medium tyres showed a +6.313 s pace delta on lap 19, then recovered to -1.116 s by lap 22 as the track cooled to 22.1 °C. Stress remained low (no reading) and the driver stayed in P5‑P4. The modelled degradation stayed flat, indicating the large slowdown was purely grip‑related; an early switch to intermediates at lap 27 avoided further loss.

findings.headline: High stress on lap 28 under blue flag – brief focus cue may unlock tyre potential
findings.detail: Stress rose to 67.4 on lap 28 while on fresh intermediates (age 2) in heavy wet and a blue‑flag situation. Pace delta was 0.000 s, but the model suggests the tyres were still gaining grip (modelled deg -0.072 s/lap). The driver’s fatigue rating (Tired) and blue‑flag traffic likely limited exploitation of the tyre advantage; consider a brief driver‑focus reminder when blue‑flags appear on wet tyres.

findings.headline: Stress fell as track warmed – driver adapted well to wet intermediates
findings.detail: From lap 31 to 38 stress dropped from 44.9 to 18.5 while on intermediates (age 5‑12) and the track warmed from 20.7 °C to 23.8 °C. Pace delta stayed around 0 s, and the modelled degradation remained slight (-0.072 s/lap). The decreasing stress suggests the driver adapted to wet conditions; no action needed but note the positive adaptation for future wet‑to‑dry phases.

findings.headline: Very high stress on lap 45 despite stable pace – schedule post‑race aero check
findings.detail: Stress peaked at 83.2 on lap 45 while on hard tyres (age 7) in wet conditions and a blue‑flag situation. Pace delta was +0.000 s, but the model shows a slight negative degradation (-0.036 s/lap) meaning the hard tyre was still performing. The high stress may be linked to perceived front‑left damage on cars ahead. Recommend a quick visual check of front‑left aero after the race to confirm driver perception.

findings.headline: Post‑race stress 90 not relevant to lap performance
findings.detail: The final lap shows a post‑race stress reading of 90.0, not an in‑lap value, so it cannot be linked to performance. No actionable insight for race pace.
